What is Eclipsed Realms?

A world where every kind of power leaves evidence behind.

Eclipsed Realms is an open-zone action RPG about surviving a realm whose religions, monsters, cities and magic all grew around the remains of one ancient failure. Fight with steel, bows, shields, stealth and ritual magic. Build relationships through cruelty, cunning or compassion. Earn trust from factions that do not agree on what salvation looks like. Decide what you are willing to spend—stamina, blood, reputation or permanent corruption—to keep moving.

Weapons, stamina, timing and positioning define the fight.

Holy, Blood and Dark power demand different sacrifices.

Karma, faction standing and personal relationships remember different choices.

Settlements, wilderness and buried spaces share one fractured history.

I

The Story

A prison made from six anchors.

The story begins with the aftermath of the First Binding: an ancient act of containment whose failure shaped the land long before the player awakened inside it.

The realm inherited the ritual. It did not inherit the whole truth.

Foundational Event

The First Binding

The wound beneath every kingdom

Purpose

Containment

Structure

Six blood anchors

Condition

Fractured

Legacy

Magic leaks through the broken geometry

Six anchors were joined through blood to create a prison for something that could not be destroyed. The Binding transformed place, sacrifice and ritual into a single geometry. For a time, it held.

Then the seal cracked. Its structure remains embedded in the realm, but its purpose no longer functions cleanly. Holy practice, blood rites and dark corruption are separate traditions built around contact with that broken design.

Every major power has inherited a fragment of the truth. None of them can claim the whole of it.

The Ossuary

One of the Cult arena's victims awakens in a pile of bodies beneath an old house near the Start Village. The house predates both the current village and the modern Cult; practitioners of Holy, Blood and Dark rites once used it.

The Relief

The priest finds the Relief after being unknowingly led to it by the Doll. The discovery connects the mystery beneath the house to a form of magic that must be carried, placed and used.

The Six Demons

The Nun summoned the six Greater Flesh Demons in the Cult arena. Captives are forced through them in sequence, turning the arena into an ordeal almost nobody survives—and placing the Nun at the center of the larger demonic story.

The Other Survivor

The Cult claims another person survived and sends the player toward him. The player can approach the encounter as rescue, execution or investigation, but the stranger dies regardless.

The Kingdom

What the player has done—and who is still willing to stand with them—determines whether the Cult, the Kingdom or the Hidden Village can shape the final crisis.

Eclipsed Realms gives the player control over motive, allegiance, relationships and consequence. It does not promise that every death can be prevented or every tragedy can be erased. The stranger's death is fixed; the meaning of that death, what the player learns, and who judges the choice remain variable.

The endings follow the same principle. Faction strength and the player's moral direction determine whether the Cult takes the Kingdom, the Cult is destroyed while the Kingdom remains unchanged, or the Hidden Village is able to help save it.

II

People of the Realm

Meet the figures who recognize the survivor.

Each profile presents what can be known without giving away the revelation at the center of the game.

Custom protagonist · Survivor

The Player

A life the ossuary failed to keep

Origin

Unknown at awakening

Last ordeal

Victim of the Cult arena

Disposition

Cruel · Cunning · Compassionate

Allegiance

Chosen through play

The player was one of the Cult arena's victims and awakens among bodies beneath the old house. Surviving what almost nobody survives turns the protagonist into a question every major power wants answered.

The player begins without a predetermined morality or class. Character creation defines appearance. Weapons, armor, skill investment and Relief choices define how that character acts under pressure.

Dialogue develops three personality traits. Cruel, Cunning and Compassionate answers affect relationships and strengthen the corresponding part of the character's social identity. Clothing can reinforce those traits, making presentation part of the build.

Priest · Start Village

The Priest

The man who finds the Relief

Discovery

Finds the Relief

Conviction

“Murder saves”

Gift

Creates waypoints

Service

Reduces Dark Points while willing

The priest finds the Relief. What he does not understand is that the Doll has led him to it, using his doubt and growing disillusionment to bring an ancient ritual object back into the world.

His crisis hardens into a theology built around the belief that murder saves. Yet his path is not fixed: the player may redeem him, darken him, fight him or still need the old knowledge he carries.

He can create waypoint symbols and remove Dark Points while he remains willing to help. Both services depend on the player's relationship with him.

Former healer · Witch / Nun settlement

The Nun

She summoned the six Greater Flesh Demons

Before

Healer among plague and mass death

Defining act

Summoned the six Greater Flesh Demons

Condition

Stranded between life and death

Before she became the Nun, she was a healer who remained untouched by sickness while tending the dying. Prolonged contact with death and Communion carried her beyond the Veil and left her suspended between states, still wearing the identity of the woman she had been.

She is the one who summoned the six Greater Flesh Demons into the Cult arena. That act makes her far more than the authority who handles karma and repentance: it ties her directly to the ordeal that consumes the arena's captives and to the deeper threat surrounding Demon Father.

Conscious vessel · Dark Communion

The Doll

She is already waiting at the next symbol

Made by

Ancestors of the Hidden Village

Contained

Dark Communion

Known limit

Cannot be defeated at waypoint encounters

Behavior

Controls where confrontation occurs

The ancestors of the Hidden Village once practiced Holy, Blood and Dark Communion. When they realized something within Dark Communion was becoming aware, they isolated it inside the Doll. Then the vessel became conscious.

She now appears where the ancient network touches the present. She leads the Priest to a Relief without revealing her hand, cannot be defeated at waypoint encounters and later moves confrontation to an arena on her own terms.

No confirmed portrait

Stranger · Claimed survivor

The Other Survivor

A choice whose outcome cannot be owned

Connection

Unknown to the player

Source

The Cult's claim

Fate

Dies regardless of approach

The Cult insists another person survived and sends the player to find him. He is a stranger whose existence may explain something about the player—or expose a lie surrounding the original event.

The player can arrive with mercy, violence or suspicion. His death remains inevitable. What changes is the reason the player came, what was learned, and what the decision reveals to every faction watching.

III

Places

Every settlement grew over an older layer.

The realm moves from lived-in villages and controlled city districts to ritual arenas, flooded underways and structures built for the dead.

Settlement · Early social hub

Start Village

Ordinary life beside an extraordinary grave

Landmark

The old house

Key figure

The priest

Hidden layer

Ossuary

The Start Village grounds the opening in work, worship, neighbors and local loyalties. It is also built beside evidence that the land was used long before the settlement understood itself as a village.

The house above the ossuary predates the present Cult and village. Holy, Blood and Dark practitioners all passed through its history, making the player's origin inseparable from the three traditions that will define the wider journey.

Hidden faction territory

Hidden Village

A faith that survived outside the walls

Modern tradition

Druidic and Holy

Buried history

All three forms of Communion

Political role

Potential ally of the Kingdom

The Hidden Village preserves an alternative culture with its own architecture, armor, rites and understanding of the realm's condition. Its ancestors once knew Holy, Blood and Dark Communion—and created the Doll when they tried to contain the awareness growing inside the Dark.

That history makes the Village more than a clean “good magic” faction. Its people know what the other factions are touching because their own ancestors helped shape the danger. If the player earns the right alliances, they can still become the force capable of helping save the Kingdom.

Kingdom city · Urban open zone

The City

Law above, hunger below

Districts

Upper and Lower

Night rule

Curfew

Below

Prison and sewer routes

The City compresses wealth, law, poverty, military order and decay behind the same walls. Upper and Lower districts create different rhythms and social pressures, while guards enforce a curfew that changes how the streets function after dark.

The City's clean map is incomplete. Its prison reaches downward, the Thieves occupy sewer routes, and older structures complicate every official claim of control.

Gothic settlement · Witch / Nun territory

Cathedral Village

Where repentance becomes authority

Center

Gothic cathedral

Power

Repentance and summoning

Faction

Witch / Nun

The cathedral dominates this settlement both physically and spiritually. Its people follow a severe interpretation of faith, wrongdoing and intervention that does not align neatly with the Start Village priest or the Hidden Village.

The Nun's presence turns the area into more than a place of worship. Her history as a healer, her altered state and her creation of the six arena demons connect this settlement to the story's deepest supernatural conflict.

Cult territory · Ritual settlement

Cultist Village

Forbidden practice made public

Roman-inspired colosseum

Practice

Blood rites and summoning

Threat

Organized Cult power

The Cultist Village is not a scattering of hidden worshippers. It is a territory with infrastructure, memory and enough power to turn ritual into spectacle. Its community has grown into ruins that still carry the weight of an older age.

The colosseum is both landmark and instrument. The Nun's six demons turn it into a lethal sequence for captives; the Doll later mirrors its logic in an arena of her own and chooses where the player must meet her.

Connected subterranean spaces

Beneath the Realm

Sewers, prison, ossuary and dark dungeon

Residents

Thieves and prisoners

Routes

Hidden and unofficial

Spaces

Sewer · Prison · Ossuary · Dark Dungeon

Underground spaces are a second map of the realm. The Thieves turn flooded tunnels into territory. The prison extends the Kingdom's authority below the City. Ossuaries and dark dungeons expose structures that belong to an older order entirely.

Mountain passes and gothic corridors serve as transitions into these harsher spaces, carrying the player away from safe roads and toward the architecture of confinement, death and ritual.

IV

The Three Reliefs

Write the name. Place the symbol. Pay the cost.

Magic is a physical ritual. The player throws a Relief to create an influence zone, summons the Spirit Board, and writes the spell's name in blood before the effect manifests from the Relief.

Carry a Relief

Holy, Blood and Dark Reliefs are separate weapons with separate ability sets.

Claim the ground

Throwing the Relief creates an influence zone roughly twenty feet across.

Write the spell

Letters appear in sequence, turning cast time into a visible ritual.

Accept the cost

The tradition determines whether the spell consumes stamina, health or permanent corruption.

Restoration · Protection · Control

Holy Relief

Survival bought with endurance

Cost

Stamina

Identity

Defensive control

Risk

Leaves the body unable to fight or flee

HealRestore the caster's health.

LockRestrict nearby enemies and create recovery space.

ArmorApply major damage reduction for a limited period.

Full HealCommit to a high-tier restoration.

UltimateChannel extreme protection with healing over time.

Enhancement · Bleeding · Rupture

Blood Relief

Momentum purchased from the body

Health + Stamina

Aggressive pressure

Power makes the caster easier to kill

Blood RainIncrease damage by approximately twenty-five percent.

Area BleedSpread sustained damage through a group.

Drain / RuptureBreak down enemies across an area and reclaim momentum.

Blood MeteorDeliver the tradition's largest direct destructive effect.

UltimateTurn survival resources into overwhelming offense.

Evasion · Force · Control · Summoning

Dark Relief

Immediate power, permanent evidence

Dark Points

Threshold

100 points

Cleansing

A willing priest

InvisibilityDisappear for a cost of 1 Dark Point.

Radial PushbackDisplace nearby enemies for 2 Dark Points.

Control / FearInterfere with enemy will for 3 Dark Points.

Flesh DemonSummon forbidden power for 15 Dark Points.

CorruptionDark Points persist until a willing priest removes them.

Spirit Board

The casting focus is also a weapon.

Summoning the Board changes the character's combat state. Ordinary attacks become close-range strikes, Relief-specific actions replace the usual attack behavior, and the four learned spells sit on the face buttons while the spell modifier is held. LB + RB commits the current ultimate.

Instant spells

One-second lockout

Cast spells

Locked until the cast ends

Relief movement

Recall and throw again

Progression

Four tiers, ultimate and branching passives

V

Combat & Builds

Readable, decisive and built around stamina.

Combat aims for the physical readability of an action RPG while keeping the freedom to combine weapons, stealth, armor, social traits and magic without selecting a permanent class.

Weapon families

Choose a rhythm, not a label.

One-handed sword and shield, daggers, two-handed weapons, bows and shield-focused play occupy distinct timings and combat roles. A dagger deals less damage per strike but recovers quickly. A bow creates lethal pressure at range. Heavy attacks reward a larger commitment.

Stamina is the combat economy

Attacking, shooting, blocking and dodging all draw from the same resource. Capacity and regeneration shape how long any martial style can control a fight.

Damage remains legible

The current baseline begins around 100 player health. Representative values place a medium one-handed light hit near 55, a heavy hit near 85 and a bow hit near 70, keeping individual attacks meaningful.

Recovery requires action

Health persists after combat. Food and drink restore it over time, water supports stamina, brewed drinks offer regeneration or resistance, and Holy magic provides immediate recovery at a stamina cost.

Defense is timing

Blocking and dodging protect through resource management and timing. A shield-parry concept adds a narrow stagger window for players who commit to precise defense.

Stealth & Critical Strikes

Critical chance accelerates near mastery.

Stealth feeds a deliberately skewed critical curve. Early investment produces modest gains; the increase becomes more pronounced near 100 stealth. The target cap is 35% critical chance at 100 stealth with 1.5× critical damage.

Crouching adds 5 stealth.

Stealth Training has five ranks, each adding 10 stealth.

Thief gear adds 2 stealth per piece; caster gear adds 1 per piece.

Knight, Templar and Guard armor impose increasingly serious stealth penalties.

Armor & Equipment

Mixed sets are part of the build.

Bonuses are applied per piece across five equipment slots. A player can combine Knight plate, Druid equipment, Thief leather and caster pieces instead of waiting for a complete-set rule to recognize the build.

Each Druid piece targets +20% maximum stamina and +10% stamina regeneration.

Thief pieces add direct stealth support.

Caster pieces provide a lighter stealth contribution.

Military armor trades concealment for direct combat identity.

Progression

The world scales selectively.

Levels run from 1 to 100, with the broader health curve moving from roughly 100 HP toward 1000 HP. Rewards account for enemy level and difficulty, targeting approximately ten appropriate fights per level.

Combat, Sneak, Speech and Fortitude form the core skills.

Trash, mid-tier and boss enemies use increasing reward multipliers.

Dungeons scale to remain relevant.

Ambient low-level enemies remain weak enough to show the player's growth.

Controller language

Combat stays under the player's hands.

The standard layout keeps defense, attacks, interaction and movement consistent while the Spirit Board changes the meaning of combat inputs when it is equipped.

LT

Block

RT

Light / Heavy attack

LB

Ability wheel

RB

Special action

LB + RB

Ultimate

Y

Charge / summon Board by context

X · A · B

Interact · Jump · Crouch

D-pad

Inventory left · Map right

With the Spirit Board active, the face buttons become the learned Relief spells while the spell modifier is held; ordinary attack inputs become punches and Relief-specific actions.

VI

Factions & Consequence

No single score can explain who trusts you.

Karma, faction reputation and personal relationships track different kinds of consequence. Helping a faction can still be cruel. Acting compassionately can still create an enemy.

Karma

A negative-to-positive record of broad moral consequence. Extreme positions affect judgment, access and hostility. The nun's repentance addresses this burden.

Faction Standing

Separate reputations for the Start Village, Hidden Village, Cult, Kingdom and Witch / Nun faction. Extremes can lead to bans, hostility or privileged access.

Relationships

Individual people respond to the personality and history of the player. Matching their preferred disposition strengthens the bond; repeated mismatch can damage it.

Home

Start Village

Villagers, local loyalties and the priest who connects everyday life to the ancient waypoint network.

Values

Community · Survival · Local trust

Risk

Losing the first place willing to shelter you

Hidden

Druids & Holy Tradition

A culture outside Kingdom authority whose endurance and old knowledge can become decisive in the final conflict.

Old faith · Nature · Endurance

Reward

A powerful ally for the Kingdom's survival

Cult

The Cult

An organized power that treats bloodshed as devotion and the arena as proof of strength. It inherited dangerous rites without understanding every force behind them.

Creed

Blood wins favor · Strength proves worth

Ambition

Control of the Kingdom

Kingdom

Crown, Guards & Citizens

The realm's civic and military authority: nobles above, labor below, guards in the streets and a prison beneath them all.

Order · Law · Continuity

Weakness

Institutions built over truths they do not control

Witch / Nun

The Cathedral Authority

A severe religious power shaped by the Nun's passage from healer to something caught between life and death.

Center

Gothic Cathedral

Service

Karma repentance

Thieves

The Thieves

A criminal faction built around routes, rooms and knowledge the Kingdom cannot fully patrol.

Access · Secrecy · Survival

Territory

The sewer network

The realm's violence has human and inhuman faces. Eclipsed Realms

VII

Enemies & Threats

The realm's violence has human and inhuman faces.

Some threats are creatures shaped by the realm's corruption. Others are people defending territory, enforcing law or following an allegiance the player has chosen to oppose.

When the trees go quiet, the silhouette is already close.

Wilderness predator · Inhuman threat

Wendigos

Antlered horrors beyond the safe roads

Range

Forests and ruined wilds

Known lair

Wendigo cave

Silhouette

Tall, horned and unmistakable

Encounter

Close-range wilderness threat

Relief link

Blood

Wendigos are among the realm's defining nonhuman enemies: towering, antlered predators that turn travel through the forest into an encounter with something physically overwhelming.

Their cave is tied to the discovery of the Blood Relief, binding this creature threat directly to the player's magical progression rather than leaving it as a detached wilderness encounter.

The Cult arena

The Six Demons

The Nun summoned all six Greater Flesh Demons. Once-human vessels, they have been fed by the arena's repeated deaths across generations. The Cult forces captives through them in sequence, and almost nobody survives the full ordeal.

Made through Communion

Flesh Demons

Lesser and Greater forms are created through forbidden practice. Lesser forms can eventually be summoned by the player; the Greater forms define the arena's major confrontations.

Human ritualists

Cultists

Their creed makes killing an act of devotion and survival proof of worth. Their danger comes from organization, blood rites and confidence that sacrifice earns favor.

Wilderness

Corrupted Beasts

Forest life reshaped into grotesque evidence that the realm's corruption reaches beyond human belief.

Conditional hostility

Druids

The Hidden Village can stand beside the player or against them. Conflict grows from choices, reputation and territory—not from a blanket rule that every faction is an enemy.

Law and military power

Knights & Guards

The Kingdom's armed authority enforces its streets, borders and curfew. Whether they are protectors or opponents depends on what the player has done.

Under-city faction

Thieves

The sewer network gives the Thieves routes, concealment and territory beyond the Kingdom's cleanest maps.

VIII

The Living World

Travel, time and preparation carry consequences too.

Exploration connects open zones, settlements, dungeons and transitional spaces while keeping repeated travel generous once the player has earned familiarity with a route.

Day & Night

The world keeps a longer rhythm.

The cycle uses a 14-hour daylight and 10-hour night proportion, stretched so the sun's movement feels gradual. Darkness changes more than lighting: the City's curfew alters access, safety and the meaning of being outside after hours.

Ancient symbols become a modern road.

Discovered waypoints allow unlimited fast travel. The Start Village priest can create new symbols, connecting a convenience system directly to the lore of the broken Binding.

Roads still matter before they become familiar.

A mount supports long distances. Swimming, ladders and cover open alternate paths through settlements, wilderness and interiors. Indoor and outdoor navigation share the minimap system.

Challenge lives where it belongs.

Dungeons scale and respawnable challenge spaces preserve difficult combat. Ambient low-tier enemies remain low enough for progression to feel real.

What you carry changes the next fight.

Food heals over time. Water supports stamina. Brewed drinks add regeneration and resistance. Relief choice, armor pieces and weapon family determine which risks the player is prepared to take.

01 / World & story

The seal is broken. The reckoning begins.

You awaken in a torture dungeon, a survivor of the Cult’s machinery. Your memories are fragments. Beyond the walls, an ancient seal has fractured—and magic is leaking into the world.

The First Binding

A prison made with blood.

The First Binding failed. Six anchors formed a prison, but its seal could not hold. What escaped now reaches into places, people and the powers they wield.

Your journey begins among the consequences of that failure. The choice is whether to resist the corruption—or use it.

The cathedral approachSupplied environment reference

The opening village

The first settlement beyond your escape. Meet its people and begin to understand the world you have returned to.

The Hidden Village

A secluded community tied to Druid and Holy traditions, with the Old Man and his family at the heart of its stories.

Cult territory

Dark Relief users, a colosseum and the cathedral. The Cult’s reach extends well beyond the dungeon where you awaken.

The kingdom

Upper and lower districts, royal power, guards, curfew and a prison. What the city permits is not always what it forgives.

The Witch Priest’s village

A settlement connected to the healer known as the Witch Priest, with its own people, beliefs and place in the story.

The sewers

Below the city, the thieves have their own territory and loyalties. The kingdom looks different from underneath.

The Cursed Doll

A strange guide bound to ancient symbols. Her role reaches into travel, Dark Communion and the Training Arena.

Main Priest

A Holy figure connected to Relief magic and the waypoints that help you navigate the realm.

Witch Priest

A plague-resistant healer whose place in the main story extends far beyond a single village.

The Old Man

A Holy Relief user in the Hidden Village. His trust opens the way to deeper lessons.

The royal court

King Melato, Queen Sicilian and the kingdom’s Blood mage occupy the center of royal power.

The Jester

At the Opera Hall, completed quests can become performances—stories you may step into again.

A story to discover

Follow a crying boy through the forest. Earn the Old Man’s trust. Learn why the Doll is waiting. The people you encounter lead you into quests whose full consequences belong in the game.

02 / Combat & character growth

Steel when words fail. A character shaped by you.

Build a fighting style around your weapons, techniques and Relief school. Choose your starting attributes and personality, then grow through skills and upgrades.

Make the opening.

Close-range attacks, bows and Relief magic offer different approaches to an encounter. Weapon techniques give you a dedicated move beyond the basic attack.

Defend with intent.

Blocking relies on stamina. A well-timed shield parry can stagger an opponent and create a chance to act.

Read the enemy.

Face ordinary enemies, bosses and elites. More dangerous opponents can change their pace as a fight turns against them.

Weapon · Its advantage

Sword · Armor penetration.

Axe · Greater bleed potential.

Dagger · Increased critical damage.

Shield · Reduced bleed taken, alongside blocking and parrying.

Two-handed weapons · Stronger versions of the corresponding weapon passive.

Begin with choices. Grow into a style.

Choose your appearance, allocate twelve starting attribute points and give your personality a head start with fifteen points in five-point steps.

Your starting selections support the character you want to play. They are followed by skill unlocks, techniques, spell upgrades and continued character growth.

Strength

Improves attack power.

Dexterity

Improves stealth.

Intelligence

Improves maximum stamina.

Vitality

Improves maximum health.

Charisma

Improves your initial standing with people and factions.

Witty

Give your character a sharper voice in conversations.

Empathetic

Make understanding others part of your approach.

Bold

Meet a conversation with confidence and willingness to take a risk.

Personality helps shape dialogue options. Some conversations offer an additional risky response.

Skills & progression

Spend points on skills, techniques and Relief abilities. New Game+ and New Game++ extend the journey and its character growth.

Equipment & survival

Manage weapons, armor, food, water and other carried items. Health, stamina, armor, attack power, stealth and critical stats inform your build.

Travel & rest

Discover waypoints, travel on foot or on horseback, and use campsites to rest, eat, save or load before continuing.

Three Reliefs. Three ways to change the fight.

Magic begins with a Relief. Wield it, deploy it, and step inside its influence to cast. Each Relief can serve one caster at a time.

The Holy Relief

A light worth holding onto.

Restore health, reinforce your defenses and hold enemies in place. Holy magic gives you the strength to endure—and the means to help others endure beside you.

Lesser Heal

A quick restoration of health.

20% → 35% health restored

Greater Heal

More powerful healing when the fight demands it.

45% → 80% health restored

Holy Armor

Strengthen your armor for the struggle ahead.

+300 → +500 armor · 20 seconds

Binding Light

Root an enemy and reclaim the moment.

5 → 8 seconds of rooting

Divine Renewal

Recover health over time.

8% → 15% health restored per second

The Blood Relief

Power always asks for something.

Turn sacrifice into strength. Drain life, surge into battle and command a demon to fight beside you. Blood magic rewards those willing to pay its price.

Offering

Trade health for greater attack power and armor.

30 → 45 seconds · attack power and armor improve

Siphon

Drain life from your enemy.

A 5-second channel · life drain improves with upgrades

Rush

Move faster and seize the opening.

+25% → +45% movement speed · 15 seconds

Rupture

Unleash damage along a forward lane.

150% → 275% of attack power

Summon Demon

Call a temporary demonic ally into the fight.

45 seconds · upgraded demon gains 75% health and damage

The Dark Relief

Let the darkness in. Feel what it takes.

Disappear from sight, turn fear against your enemies and leave them marked by a curse. Dark spells build Dark Points. At full corruption, your health and stamina suffer, and you can no longer cast Holy magic.

Invisibility

Conceal yourself from sight.

10 → 15 seconds · upgrade adds healing

Void Pulse

Push enemies away and create space.

5 → 8 meters of knockback

Fear

Send your enemy into terror.

5 → 9 seconds of fear

Curse

Wear an enemy down with damage over time.

20% → 35% of target maximum health as damage over time

Dark Continuance

Draw on the Dark for a temporary increase in power.

10 → 20 seconds · +15% → +25% attack power

Each school has five spells to unlock and upgrade, plus an ultimate ability. Values shown describe the current design and may be tuned during development.

Wield & deploy.

The appropriate Relief must be wielded to grant its abilities. Deploy it and remain within its influence to cast.

One caster at a time.

A deployed Relief serves a single user. Its influence is a place you must manage in the fight.

Commit at release.

Letters are written over the Relief as you cast. The cost and cooldown begin when the completed cast visibly releases. An interrupted cast that never releases does not spend them.

Dark Points

Power leaves a mark.

Dark spells add Dark Points. At one hundred, corruption reduces maximum health, maximum stamina and stamina regeneration by ten percent, and prevents Holy casting.

Main Priest can help reduce Dark Points. Corruption is distinct from karma: the magic you use and the choices you make are different parts of your character.

Ultimate abilities

Each Relief school has an ultimate to unlock. Learning and improving magic is part of progression through the people and quests of the realm.

04 / Choices & consequences

The world remembers who you become.

Trust, reputation, karma and corruption each track a different part of your journey. A person’s opinion of you is not interchangeable with a faction’s standing—or with the power you carry.

Trust is personal.

Each NPC can have a relationship with you. Your actions and conversations can earn their trust or give them a reason to doubt you, changing how they respond.

Loyalties carry weight.

Factions have their own standing with you. Helping one group may not make you welcome among another, and the people you encounter have reasons for their loyalties.

Your path is yours.

Karma follows your moral choices. The route toward saving the realm and the pursuit of corrupt power lead the story in different directions.

What was seen can matter later.

The consequence system accounts for witnessed actions. NPC reactions can reflect what they know, rather than treating every encounter as a fresh start.

Starting an assault and defending yourself are different situations. The design also accounts for NPC aggression toward the player.

Guards, arrest & jail

Guard responses and arrest/jail behavior are part of the consequence-system work. They extend the relationship between an incident, its witnesses and the people responsible for keeping order.

Earn the next step.

A mentor’s trust can be the difference between meeting them and learning what they have to teach.

Choose how to respond.

Personality gives conversations different voices. A witty answer, an empathetic reply or a bold response can shape the way an encounter unfolds.

Live with the result.

Quest decisions can change your path, the relationships around you and what comes next. The full outcomes belong in the story you play.

Karma & Dark Points

Karma concerns your choices. Dark Points concern your use of Dark magic. They are separate systems, each with its own consequences.

05 / Co-op, companions & arenas

Someone at your side. Someone across the arena.

Campaign co-op, dungeon allies, training and competitive arenas offer different ways to share the realm. The configurations below describe the multiplayer design targets while development continues.

Online campaign players

Explore and fight together in a campaign designed to support up to four online players.

Local co-op players

Two-player couch co-op shares the journey on the same screen.

Two households

The combined target brings two local players together with two local players online.

Final supported configurations will be confirmed as the multiplayer implementation is validated.

Four-player dungeons. More ways to find company.

Dungeons are designed around a group of four. Optional NPC helpers provide a melee fighter, a ranged fighter and a magic user, and can accompany you inside the dungeon.

Helpers join the party for the run, with their health and portrait visible. They leave after the boss is defeated or when you leave through the entrance or exit.

Three roles

Melee: a fighter for close-range pressure.

Ranged: support from a distance.

Magic: a caster alongside the group.

Dungeon allies support the run alongside your player companions.

Learn the enemies. Return to your journey.

Find the Cursed Doll near discovered waypoints and travel to the Training Arena. Practice against enemies associated with the area you came from, one at a time.

Training grants experience but no loot. Return to your origin, or travel to an origin you have already discovered through the Doll.

01Find the DollReach her in an area tied to a waypoint.

02Enter trainingFace that area’s enemies in sequence.

03Return or travelLeave for your origin or a previously discovered one.

A duel

Two-player teams

Three-player teams

Up to eight players

Competitive fights use arena sessions rather than replacing the campaign journey.

A quest becomes a performance.

Replay a completed main quest as a staged performance. The crowd may cheer or boo, but the replay carries no campaign consequences and awards no experience or loot.

Leave the performance and return to the stage when you are ready to continue your real journey.

Character motives and transformations Eclipsed Realms Storyboard

Discovery versus fast travel Keep About: discovering a region and binding its Cursed Doll are separate. Using a regional Doll to enter training binds that destination to the individual player; the Arena Doll offers bound destinations.

Cathedral, Nun and Witch Priest naming Keep neutral descriptions of the religious regions. Do not merge distinct churches or declare Witch Priest and Nun interchangeable. Gallery captions retain the supplied cathedral-reference label without confirming the final in-game location.

Lore, endings and Chapter II Merge the shared premise and neutral regional context into About. Preserve all 49 storyboard beats behind a spoiler control. Older detailed outcomes and Chapter II geography remain narrative reference; absence from About is not proof of implementation or a contradiction.

The Player: A survivor without memory who inherits the forces that damaged, protected, and seduced everyone before them. Survival → Communion → faction choice → what survives

The Doll: Dark Communion contained until it developed memory and will. It helps whenever help creates more bloodshed. Vessel → waypoints → Priest → Cult → darker path

The Nun: A healer shaped by plague, stranded between life and death, revealed through memories, consumed by final purpose. Healer → threshold → mutations → Six → sacrifice

The Priest: A believer who mistakes a real supernatural mechanism for proof that murder is divine salvation. Faith → shoreline Relief → doctrine → village → Nun

The Old Man: A practitioner who sees his wife’s death as proof that power should be abandoned. Holy magic → accidental harm → grief → withdrawal

The Mage: A son who sees the same tragedy as proof that power must be mastered completely. Hidden Village → Blood → Wendigo → royal protector

The King: A once-liked ruler whose fear creates the army, taxation, and permanent control meant to protect people. Protection → militarization → martial law → possible alliance

The Cult: Heirs to incomplete knowledge who turn reliable bloodshed into worship, society, and spectacle. Fragments → village → Arena → collapse or victory

The Hidden Village: Descendants of those who created the Doll; burdened by guilt and uniquely equipped to resist it. Three Communions → containment → secrecy → resistance

Lore and rules Eclipsed Realms Storyboard

How the campaign ending is chosen Keep About: the decisive ending is an explicit story choice, committed by the host. The Design Atlas places it at the End Church and explicitly excludes the legacy karma-threshold route. Faction relationships remain distinct.

Personality names About supplies no authoritative three-label set. Use general wording about dialogue and relationships on the main page; preserve both sets here until the project confirms the names.

Cathedral, Nun and Witch Priest naming Keep neutral descriptions of the religious regions. Do not merge distinct churches or declare Witch Priest and Nun interchangeable. Gallery captions retain the supplied cathedral-reference label without confirming the final in-game location.

Lore, endings and Chapter II Merge the shared premise and neutral regional context into About. Preserve all 49 storyboard beats behind a spoiler control. Older detailed outcomes and Chapter II geography remain narrative reference; absence from About is not proof of implementation or a contradiction.

Death, grief, bone and memory thin the damaged Veil. Ossuaries, churches, plague sites, arenas, graveyards and the Necropolis connect to this premise.

Holy, Blood and Dark are three approaches to the same wound. A Relief is the place where Communion occurs and a spell name is written.

Karma concerns moral action. Dark Points concern Dark Communion. Personality, individual relationships and faction reputation remain separate.

The older story treats the Binding, the Six, the Other Survivor’s death, mutations and the King’s army as history the player cannot simply erase.

A shared journey with personal memories. Dialogue choices shape the player; the committed ending changes the campaign.

Design intent: Keep personal reactions and one-time rewards separate from shared progression. The End Church choice decides the finale; the legacy Karma-threshold ending is not part of this route.

How it works:

Meet the Doll → leave the cage → witness the attic memory.

Reach the village → speak with the Barmaid and Priest → choose a pledge, if desired.

Survive the six-demon ordeal. Q05 can begin without the Priest.

Return to the ossuary → confront the ritual at the End Church.

Commit the good or evil route → defeat the Demon Father or the four gate defenders.

Authoring and review notes (historical documentation):

Inspect the existing open-world placements before authoring: the original wiring checklist was completed on October 3.

Edit story sources in Docs/Authoring/Story. Dialogue imports update by node ID; quest generation is create-only. Review existing quest assets before changing them.

For added story NPC placements, apply Actor Tag StoryNPC and configure Eclipsed Story > Routes. Keep travel-station dolls untagged.

Connect area overlaps through Eclipsed Story Event Trigger; connect sequence finish AND skip through a Story Sequence Hook.

Use once keys for rewards, player flags for knowledge and world flags for shared progression.

Play both endings, skip cinematics, save/reload and check a host plus guest.

Owner: StoryFlags on PlayerState; Narrative quests; campaign World Events

Network: Server writes progression. Host commits the shared ending; a guest proposes it.

Save behavior: Personal flags and once keys in player records; world flags in the campaign.

Recorded evidence: Oct 8: new-game story world 71 passed / 0 failed. Earlier story report includes explicit forced test steps; this is recorded evidence, not a new run.

Known limits:

The initial “nothing placed” statement in the first-pass report is superseded by its §6 / §9 and the session-h world integration.

Do not reconnect preserved legacy Karma-based ending events to the new route.

Jester performances Eclipsed Realms · Design Atlas

Snapshot through October 8, 2026 · 16 performances

Evidence is dated; this consolidation does not rerun gameplay tests.

Numbers, bindings and feature availability Preserve the dated values for reference; do not import them as current promises. The Atlas also records input conflicts, pending physical-controller checks and a guards-proof regression. Historical test passes do not validate today’s game build.

Replay a story you have already lived, then return with your campaign restored.

Design intent: Let players revisit completed or failed quests without keeping performance gains or losses. Co-op isolation preserves what the other players do outside the performance.

How it works:

The player opens the nearby stage’s playbill. Only completed or failed quests are eligible.

The replay definition restarts the quest and sets its curtain-up flags, destination layers and cast.

Play the actual story beats. Saving is paused while the performance runs.

Success, failure, death or Leave Performance ends it.

Solo restores the campaign checkpoint; co-op restores the performer while other players keep their progress.

Authoring and review notes (historical documentation):

Inspect Story_OperaHall_JesterStage and /Game/Story/Jester/DA_Replay_*; 16 definitions are already covered.

For a new replay, create EclipsedReplayDefinition: Quest, Replayable, Playbill Title / Description, Start From State and Start Transform.

Author CurtainClear/SetPlayerFlags, CurtainClear/SetWorldFlags and CompanionQuests to establish the intended starting beat.

Put required NPCs and props in Performance Cast. Use OnlyIfAbsentWithin for stand-ins, and bHostileOnRelease where needed.

Treat any definition touching shared world flags as alone-only. Wire Eclipsed: Open Jester Playbill into the Jester dialogue.

Test eligibility before granting history; finish, leave and die; compare canonical state after every restore.

Owner: UEclipsedJesterReplaySubsystem; ReplayDefinition; JesterStage

Network: One co-op performer at a time. Shared-world curtain changes are refused in co-op.

Save behavior: Solo verified checkpoint + crash marker; performer-scoped co-op restore. No performance rewards persist.

Recorded evidence: Oct 8: all 16 final performance runs green; each restore compared 31 canonical values. CH01’s real walk remains a separate failure.

Known limits:

CH01 used a TEST SETUP arrival stand-in; the later real-route test was 21 passed / 1 failed.

Earlier “co-op refused” and “no quests enabled” notes are superseded.

Documented command (not executed): run_jester_perform.ps1

Bind a regional doll by using it, enter training, then choose a bound doll on the world map.

Design intent: Discovery and travel permission are different. Discovering a region reveals its doll; using that doll to enter the arena binds it to that player.

How it works:

Regional dialogue fires NE_ER_TravelToTrainingArena and registers the source doll.

The player arrives at the Arena Doll after the travel transition.

NE_ER_OpenCursedDollTravelMap opens Narrative’s map for that player.

Bound dolls are selectable; discovered but unbound dolls are dimmed.

The server checks the player’s location and binding before travel.

Authoring and review notes (historical documentation):

Inspect existing stations first; the manuals document a test-map foundation, not a complete regional placement inventory.

For a new regional doll, place Eclipsed Cursed Doll Station beside it. Set unique Doll Id, Regional role, Associated POI and Training Profile.

Position Arrival P1, Arrival P2 and Arrival Emergency; put the Safety Floor just beneath them.

Apply Cursed Doll Icon To POI, then run Map Check / Data Validation.

Place or inspect the TrainingArena-role station with DL_TrainingArena.

Wire regional dialogue to NE_ER_TravelToTrainingArena; Arena dialogue to NE_ER_OpenCursedDollTravelMap and optionally NE_ER_ReturnFromTrainingArena.

Test bound/unbound choices, cancel, save/restore and separate-player travel; manually test mouse selection.

Owner: AEclipsedCursedDollStation; UEclipsedCursedDoll subsystem

Network: Per-player map and travel. Server validates each destination.

Save behavior: Bindings per player. Loading an arena save returns to the source doll.

Recorded evidence: Session h: Doll / Training / fog-exclusion route 39/0. Session g: solo, couch and remote-client doll-map proofs.

Known limits:

Mouse doll-marker selection was not automated in session g.

Fight copies of real enemies, gain normal XP, and leave the world’s history untouched.

Design intent: Training uses production stats, equipment, abilities and AI, but excludes loot, crime, karma, persistent world memory and quest kill credit.

How it works:

The source doll selects the regional Training Profile.

Hold Interact for one second on Start Training.

The director spawns training copies and tracks their summons.

Kills grant XP; other world consequences and loot are excluded.

All participants down or the last player leaving resets only the run’s actors.

Authoring and review notes (historical documentation):

Open /Game/Maps/DevMaps/L_EclipsedCursedDollTest to inspect the working fixture.

In DL_TrainingArena, place Eclipsed Training Start Point beside the Arena Doll.

Set the Arena station’s Enemy Spawn Points and Arena Respawn Delay (documented default: 3 seconds).

Duplicate DA_ER_Training_CultVillage for a new region; list every real NPC definition needed and assign the profile to its station.

Optionally wire NE_ER_StartTraining into the Arena Doll dialogue.

Verify XP is granted but loot, karma, crimes and quest kills are not; die, leave, and save/reload.

Owner: EclipsedTrainingRun director and profile assets

Network: Arena presentation is per view / per machine. Online clients prepare copies from listed profiles.

Save behavior: Training enemies are not restored. Loading returns the player to the source doll.

Recorded evidence: Session g: training run 23/0; fresh restore 2/0 + 2/0. Packaged Development run 23/0.

Witnesses & consequences Eclipsed Realms · Design Atlas

Snapshot through October 8, 2026 · Runtime proven

Numbers, bindings and feature availability Preserve the dated values for reference; do not import them as current promises. The Atlas also records input conflicts, pending physical-controller checks and a guards-proof regression. Historical test passes do not validate today’s game build.

NPC individuals remember what they actually witnessed. One attack event creates one updating consequence card.

Design intent: Keep crime evidence, personal memory and player-facing feedback consistent. Two guards of one definition remain two distinct witnesses.

How it works:

An attack creates incidents grouped by player and damage source.

Eligible individual witnesses record the event according to awareness rules.

Karma / faction effects follow incident rules; newly hostile NPCs are identified.

One card updates in place as later witnesses are confirmed.

Remembered incidents inform later conversations and may reach law enforcement.

Authoring and review notes (historical documentation):

Tune Project Settings > Game > Eclipsed Consequences: AssaultGroupingSeconds (3 seconds) and FeedEntrySeconds (12 seconds).

Author social identities and ties through NPC definitions and the awareness Ties asset.

Keep per-instance witness identity intact; do not regenerate production NPC IDs to solve card counts.

Attack near two same-definition guards, repeat a hit and introduce a late witness. Check one updated card with distinct remembered individuals.

Save and reload, then test the second couch player’s separate card and memory.

Give guards, villagers, knights and thieves distinct responses without changing their factions.

Design intent: Reusable response categories provide direct-hit, witnessed-assault and remembered-assault lines, with variation between nearby speakers.

How it works:

Assign a Response Category explicitly or match a rule by definition.

The server selects a variant for the situation and keeps its context.

Nearby speakers avoid the same variant; an NPC avoids its previous one.

Spoken lines use Narrative’s dialogue position, queue during conversations and avoid duplicates.

Remembered-assault dialogue offers apology, self-defence claim, threat or leave.

Authoring and review notes (historical documentation):

Edit Docs/Authoring/Responses/Categories/<Category>.json and the corresponding Dialogues JSON.

Run EclipsedTools.ImportResponseCategories from Session Frontend > Automation.

Assign NPC Definition > Social > Dialogue > Response Category, or add a category rule under Eclipsed NPC Responses.

Use CharacterIds / DefinitionNameContains and Priority to control matching.

Test two adjacent guards and a villager, then revisit remembered conversations and check simultaneous subtitle spacing.

Owner: UEclipsedResponseCategory; SocialModules; SocialNotices

Network: Server selects the line; clients display the result.

Save behavior: Persistent memories come from consequences; categories are authored data.

Recorded evidence: Session h: responses 24/0 in editor and package.

Known limits:

Categories are not factions. An uncategorized NPC retains its existing behavior.

A witnessed or reported illegal act can lead to confrontation, bribery, arrest and custody.

Design intent: Law consumes existing evidence; it does not invent witnesses. Jurisdiction policy defines arrestable actions and server-owned cases drive the response.

How it works:

An identified enforcer witnesses a crime, or receives a report.

The Kingdom policy judges the act and the law subsystem opens a response.

Dialogue offers applicable accept, refuse and bribe outcomes.

Custody uses jail cells and a belongings chest; protected quest items stay with the player.

Standing, custody and belongings persist in the player’s own law record.

Authoring and review notes (historical documentation):

Inspect Project Settings > Eclipsed Law: open-world enablement, jurisdictions, enforcers and royals.

Inspect existing Kingdom_Cell2 / 3 / 5 / 6 and Kingdom_BelongingsChest in the city dungeon.

After moving the dungeon, rerun EclipsedTools.Law.KingdomCells. For new cells, set unique CellId, Jurisdiction, door width, escort acceptance and interior layers; local +X points out.

Author confrontation in Docs/Authoring/Law/Law_Confrontation.json; use NC_ER_LawCanBribe and NE_ER_LawAccept/Refuse/Pay.

Protect required quest items with Eclipsed.Item.KeepOnArrest or KeepOnArrestClasses.

Test arrest, bribe, refusal, reinforcement, persistence and a remote client before extending a jurisdiction.

Players and NPCs mount through Narrative interaction; riding orders coordinate NPC travel.

Design intent: Keep riders seated consistently across the network, prevent weapon use while mounted, and make dismounting a controlled stop.

How it works:

Interact with a horse; weapons are put away before mounting.

The rider controls movement or follows an NPC Ride To order.

Remote players and late joiners see the rider attached at saddle height.

Hold Interact to brake and then dismount.

An NPC returns to its normal AI after the order finishes or is cancelled.

Authoring and review notes (historical documentation):

Use an existing NPC_Horse / BP_EclipsedHorse; no new player-mount actor is required.

For an NPC route, call the latent Blueprint node Eclipsed NPC Ride To with NPC, Mount and Destination.

Handle Arrived / Failed or the Ride Order On Finished result; handle competing claims and cancellations.

Ride, gallop, steer and hold Interact to dismount; test with a remote rider and a late joiner.

Test couch player 2 leaving while mounted and verify the horse remains.

Owner: HorseLocomotion; MountRider; NPCRiding; RideOrder

Network: Server decides mount / dismount and claims. Remote attachment and animation are synchronized.

Save behavior: Uses existing character / mount lifecycle; inspect current manual for tested restore paths.

Presentation closes, appropriate pause state clears and TravelFinished fires.

Share the world while keeping each player’s character, knowledge, UI and saved progress distinct.

Design intent: Stable save identity must survive display-name changes, campaign loads and reconnects. Couch players get their own input, menus and records.

How it works:

Online guests join the host; a second local pad presses Start on a gameplay map.

Each player gets an owning view, UI and stable identity; LocalP2 is scoped to the campaign slot.

Save writes the world and player records; the selected slot becomes the active campaign.

Host Load restores listening; online guests reconnect after the map change.

Couch player 2 pauses and holds View / Back for 1.5 seconds to save and leave.

Authoring and review notes (historical documentation):

Connect two physical controllers and start a gameplay map. Pad 2 Start joins; keyboard / mouse and pad 1 remain player 1.

Open each player’s menu and verify input never moves the other player’s focus.

Leave with pad 2 Start then hold View / Back; rejoin and verify character and inventory.

Save from the pause menu, close and reload; verify standalone player-2 persistence.

Host online, join with a different profile, change campaign slot, load and reconnect.

For a new guest appearance, use Create Character + Join in the multiplayer menu; cancel should cancel the join.

Owner: CouchCoop; SaveSubsystem; HostContinuity; SplitScreenScaler

Network: Only the host machine can add a couch player; maximum two local players.

Save behavior: One file per player. Standalone couch persistence is fixed in session h.

Recorded evidence: Session g packaged couch 75/0; Shipping smoke 13/0. Session h confirms fresh-process standalone P2 restore.

Known limits:

Physical pads remain untested; automated input was injected at Slate entry points.

Unplugging pad 2 mid-game is not handled in the session-g handoff.

The older “use ?listen for P2 saves” limitation is superseded.

The director locks doors, enables containment, reveals the crowd and starts storm events.

Each stage summons a demon; actual defeated stages advance the shared objective.

Six defeats complete Q05 and begin the next story beat.

Saved progress resumes at the next demon; a completed encounter does not restart.

Assign spectators, summon effects / sounds and start / end weather events.

Network: Shared encounter and objective; trigger should be inside containment.

Save behavior: Defeated count is a world fact; completion is the encounter’s World Event tag.

For a product build, use EclipsedRealms, never the EclipsedRealmsSmoke test target.

What happens to progress? Eclipsed Realms · Design Atlas

Preserved from the Atlas’s progress explainer and story view; no game simulation or test was executed.

Numbers, bindings and feature availability Preserve the dated values for reference; do not import them as current promises. The Atlas also records input conflicts, pending physical-controller checks and a guards-proof regression. Historical test passes do not validate today’s game build.

Training kill, any mode: normal XP; no loot, karma, crime, witness/world memory or quest kill credit. Training copies and summons belong to the run.

Solo Jester performance: restore the verified campaign checkpoint, including XP, items, quests, world flags and canonical state.

Co-op Jester performance: isolate and restore the performer while other players retain their progress. Saving is paused for everyone; replays that change shared world flags are refused.

Online guest ending choice: the guest proposes a route; the host must confirm it at the altar. A proposal does not commit the shared ending.

Host or solo ending choice: commit the route once. Shared quests advance and the deciding player receives the one-time karma consequence.

Load in solo: restore campaign and player records. An arena save returns to its source Doll.

Load as host: reload while retaining hosting; online guests reconnect and restore their own records. Standalone local player two has a saved file.

An early pledge and the final End Church commitment are different decisions. Q05 can begin without the Priest.

The playbill’s alone/co-op labels apply to replays, not normal campaign play. Developer-granted history is not player eligibility. Legacy and test-map quests are not the production replay roster.

How later handoffs changed the plan Eclipsed Realms · Design Atlas

October 11 Atlas assembly · documentation through October 8.

Numbers, bindings and feature availability Preserve the dated values for reference; do not import them as current promises. The Atlas also records input conflicts, pending physical-controller checks and a guards-proof regression. Historical test passes do not validate today’s game build.

October 1 (sessions e/f): techniques, horses, spawners, Jester and Doll foundations; several systems were test-map only.

October 2 (session g): Doll map travel, training rules, isolated Jester co-op and couch join/leave built.

October 3 (session h and addenda): individual witnesses, response categories, fog, standalone couch persistence and story wiring in the real world.

October 8: 16 performances, travel fixes, Kingdom law, tier/input refinements; real CH01 route and V4 package remained pending.

Checklists describe repeatable authoring/review work, not missing features. Recorded passes and completion checks are historical evidence, not a live audit.

System relationships are curated design connections, not a generated code dependency graph. The original checklist contained 106 review steps; browser-local completion marks are not game state.
